subject: Post-demo: Novus Health model-fit plan + benchmark links
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Novus Health model-fit plan + benchmark links

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on the call: 

Recap:
- Scope: multi-turn clinical note summarization + sensitive PII redaction before HIE exports.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms p50 latency target for short summaries (<= 256 tokens), deterministic redaction rules, PHI never stored in hosted footprint.

Model-fit recommendations (first-pass):
1) redwood-rt-7b-int8 (recommended for pilot) — best latency/cost tradeoff for the short-summary workload. Redwood-verified profile attached.
2) open-llama-13b-q4 + structured prompt-set (higher quality on edge cases; higher cost/latency).
3) smaller distilled candidate (rw-mini-3b) for batch background jobs where throughput matters.

What I attached/linked:
- redwood-bench-20261005.csv — microbenchmark raw numbers for the models above (TPS at batch sizes 1/4/8, p50/p90/p99 latencies). [Attachment stub: 1.2MB] 
- snapshot-profile-rw-7b-int8.pdf — Redwood-verified performance profile (p50=92ms, p90=210ms, p99=430ms @ batch=1 on A10G; TPS=10 tok/s steady state).
- novus-prompt-set-v1.json — initial prompt set we used for the benchmarks (clinical templates + redaction checks).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm whether we can run a 48-hour sample on your non-prod dataset (redacted) or provide representative prompts.
- Us: run a pilot micro-benchmark with your prompts, produce a latency/TPS/quality matrix and highlight any quality/regression risks.
- Week-of-10/12: 60-minute follow-up to review pilot results and discuss Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.

Let me know if we should include your security contact on the data transfer step.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-bench-20261005.csv (text/csv)]
From: Emily Zhao <emily@novushealth.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Wu <mark.wu@novushealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Novus Health model-fit plan + benchmark links

Thanks Alex — useful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign off on a 48-hour sample run: 

1) Can you confirm the p50/p90 numbers in the PDF were measured with KV cache warm? We care a lot about first-token latency for short summaries.
2) For the redaction checks: what metric do you use to detect regression risk? We need to be able to map any quality drop to a rollback plan.
3) Data transfer: our security team prefers SFTP to a customer-managed bucket. Is that supported for a one-time ingest?

Also, curious about the TPS numbers vs the p50 — the CSV shows TPS at batch=4 that looks attractive, but we expect most of our traffic to be batch=1.

If you can answer those, we can route a small sample (de-identified) next week.

— Emily
Director of Product, Novus Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 12:18:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-demo: Novus Health model-fit plan + benchmark links

Looping you in on Emily's questions — forwarding their note. High level plan from infra/bench team: 

- Confirm KV cache pre-warm conditions (we ran the attached profile with cold-starts excluded; will reproduce both cold and warmed).
- Regression detection: we will compute precision/recall for the redaction set and flag any change >2.5% absolute as a regression candidate; also include per-example diffs and a rollout guard for canary.
- Data ingest: SFTP -> customer-managed bucket is fine; we'll provide an SFTP endpoint and an ingestion checklist (PII handling steps).

Action items for me/Dev:
- Dev: set up a micro-benchmark job that runs both cold and warm runs for rw-7b-int8 and open-llama-13b-q4; include p50/p90/p99, TPS, and the redaction precision/recall table. Attach a per-prompt trace for any failures.
- Alex: coordinate with Emily to confirm sample timing and security contact.

Forwarding with context — will track in the RWI-4391 HubSpot record.

— Lauren
Director, Solutions 
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:23:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Post-demo: Novus Health model-fit plan + benchmark links

Emily — quick follow-up with answers and concrete next steps: 

Answers: 
- KV cache: the attached rw-7b-int8 snapshot was measured with a pre-warmed cache (3 warm prompts). We'll re-run and include cold-start numbers in the micro-benchmark.
- Regression policy: as Lauren noted, we'll calculate redaction precision/recall and signpost any delta > 2.5% as a regression; we'll also surface per-example diffs so you can inspect any false negatives. Canary rollout -> automatic fallback to rw-mini-3b if degradation detected.
- Data ingest: SFTP to a customer-managed bucket is supported. I'll send an ingestion checklist + SFTP endpoint to your security contact once you confirm the point-of-contact.

Proposed schedule:
- Oct 11: we receive sample (de-identified) via SFTP.
- Oct 12–13: internal micro-benchmark runs (cold + warm), produce perf + quality matrix.
- Oct 14: 45-min review; discuss Dedicated vs Hosted for latency SLAs.

Attachments included again for convenience: redwood-bench-20261005.csv, novus-prompt-set-v1.json, snapshot-profile-rw-7b-int8.pdf.

If that timing works, reply with the security contact and approximate size of the sample. We'll also open a HubSpot activity on RWI-4391 and assign CS to support pilot onboarding.

Appreciate it — Alex
[Attachment: novus-prompt-set-v1.json (application/json)]
